PK-01: Push the generation/implementation branch after every commit that ends a sub-phase or step; never end a turn with `git log origin/<branch>..HEAD` non-empty.
D-029; S-000 (resume check); every S-### `Checkpoint` line
PK-02: S-000 clones qualitycoding/Lessons and qualitycoding/knowledge, lists the lessons matching the task tags and records the commits read before any delivery work.
PK-03: Commit once per plan step; rewrite .checkpoints/state.json in that commit; append EXECUTION_LOG.md; open DEVIATIONS.md at the first departure from the plan.
PK-04: Every number, behaviour or causal claim in code, docs or replies cites a test, spike or source opened in the same run, or carries UNVERIFIED; README sentences trace to test IDs.
PK-05: Every count in a report, prompt or status header is generated by a command, never typed.
tools/gen/*; Phase 5 status header generated by tools/gen/status.py; S-RETRO
PK-06: Label a claim corroborated only with >= 2 independent publishers (recorded as independent_publishers); facts in pinned source code are made verified by a committed spike; never cite a source not opened in this run.
PK-07: Before closing implementation, map every plan step and pre-mortem control to a delivering file or test; list unmapped ones in DEVIATIONS.md.
PK-08: Stage by explicit file list, read `git diff --cached --stat` before every commit; write .gitignore before the first build; check ignored fixtures with `git check-ignore`.
PK-09: Commit every spike that backs a claim or deviation to research/spikes/<name>/ with its output; never cite /tmp.
PK-10: After any scripted edit, grep, diff or compile the target file in the same command; run each edit as its own call.
PK-11: When a tool result says NOT RUN or is empty, re-issue it before writing any closing text.
PK-12: Attach every repository with add_repo (push) before any token; never write a pasted token to disk; check git config and grep for tokens at turn end; tell the owner to revoke pasted tokens.
PK-13: Probe every external host a step, test or gate names, record results in plan/ENVIRONMENT.md and plan an alternative channel for each unreachable one.
PK-14: GitHub Actions logs/artifacts may be unreachable from the sandbox: read CI results through the API (jobs, steps, check-run annotations) and emit failures as annotations.
PK-15: A workflow that must be dispatched manually must exist on the default branch; give every dispatch input a non-empty default.
D-018 (no workflow_dispatch on the critical path)
PK-16: Parse every workflow file with a YAML loader (and actionlint where available) before marking the plan ready; take CI tool flags and action versions from the pinned source, not memory.
PK-17: Probe permissions with read endpoints only; never write to a live object to test access.
PK-18: Builds that may exceed 250 s run as `setsid nohup <cmd> > <log> 2>&1 < /dev/null &` and are polled; never a bare `&`; one target per call otherwise.
PK-19: The sandbox shell is dash: wrap brace expansion, arrays, PIPESTATUS, `time`, `[[ ]]` and process substitution in `bash -c` or a bash script, and list created trees.
HANDOFF.md §Sandbox rules; every script has `#!/usr/bin/env bash`
PK-20: Commit a bootstrap script that clones pinned dependencies and configures the test targets, and run it first in every session.
PK-21: Before freezing, run every expected value against an independent oracle and fix tests the oracle cannot pass; evaluate each assertion on a reference or analytic case.
PK-22: Before freezing a typed interface, sketch-implement every declared function against the header alone and run the frozen tests on it.
PK-23: When a constant appears in a frozen header and a frozen fixture, diff the values before freezing; run `find tests -type f` before writing the manifest.
PK-24: Never edit a frozen test or regenerate the manifest: write TEST_CHALLENGE.md and halt (Rule 2E.4); thresholds freeze only with the baseline that sets them.
PK-25: Red verification: any passing test is a defect; failure-path assertions use dedicated exception types (NotImplemented is a logic_error); classified counts must sum to the collected total.
PK-26: Tests read environment variables through an assertion naming the variable and the plan step that sets it; JSON inputs are raw string literals asserted valid first; every C-### a test cites exists.
PK-27: Test helpers that contain an algorithm state their precondition, never fall back silently, and are checked on a hand-checkable case; every parameter that defines a window or frame count gets a test of how many items it yields.
PK-28: Check each ONNX operator's schema for the target opset and run onnx.checker on every fixture graph.
PK-29: Every numeric quality or performance target is an 'unmeasured default' until a run measures it; budgets are derived from a measured reference; confirmation goes through the result gate.
PK-30: Print the unclipped peak of every render; analyse float32 buffers; put gain and a soft clip inside the shipped signal path and assert the output peak <= 1.
PK-31: Validate each DSP/metric measurement on a synthetic known-answer signal (sine for F0, known-length renders for RTF) and validate pitch trackers on hand-checked material; treat octave jumps as tracker errors.
PK-32: Any fixture that uses cents names its reference frequency explicitly (here A4 = 440 Hz, MIDI 69).
PK-33: Segment non-stationary recordings (pitch/level tracking) before analysing them; exclude transitions.
D-017 (per-note F0 scoring on voiced interior frames)
PK-34: A stochastic stage gets a test that its noise is applied at the intended scale and is reproducible from its seed.
PK-35: Run every new acceptance measure against the baseline first (guide-only render) so improvement is shown, not assumed.
PK-36: Print a key -> Hz -> cents table against 12-TET for every pitch mapping and require 0 cents error.
PK-37: Build framework glue against the pinned JUCE tag before delivering it; grep JUCE headers for every API used and static_assert the JUCE major version; declare LANGUAGES C CXX; use brace initialisation.
PK-38: The audio thread never locks, allocates or waits: lock-free hand-off of a preallocated take, and a pre-mortem lens for it.
D-022; T-030, T-031, T-032; premortem lens 'audio thread'
PK-39: UI behaviour that cannot be run in the sandbox is listed as 'implemented, unverified' and mapped to an operational test or a gate check.
PK-40: User-visible tables and defaults are defined once in code and the UI, parameters and docs are generated from that single source.
PK-41: Python environments: include the build backend in the lock, run pip-audit and a clean-room install before code is written; close every resource in finally/context managers.
PK-42: Bytes from files and devices are untrusted: parse at the boundary and raise the project's own error type.
PK-43: Long jobs are resumable from saved state, run in slices shorter than the session limit, and checked for memory headroom before starting; never two heavy jobs at once.
PK-44: Ask at intake where training compute runs and propose a free hosted default with its session limits.
PK-45: Show the owner any domain table the tests encode before freezing it, and when the owner's description conflicts with the code ask which meaning is intended.
A-005, A-012 (intake defaults adopted); G-001 confirms
PK-46: Do not describe generative audio as 'sounds like' or 'realistic' without a listening record; by-ear behaviour is UNVERIFIED until G-001.
PK-47: Before naming a toolchain version or generator, read it from the person's log; Windows VST3 system folder is not user-writable (COPY_PLUGIN_AFTER_BUILD FALSE); JUCE_VST3_CAN_REPLACE_VST2=0.
PK-48: When fixing a project that has a named repository, clone it first and compare; before adding a module grep for one with the same responsibility.
PK-49: After a push made by a non-git mechanism, fetch and reset to the remote tip; before a history rewrite use an explicit lease; shallow clones fetch the default branch before pushing.
PK-50: List every licence file the plan needs and check its text is obtainable; include a LICENSE in the first push.
PK-51: After any fix to shared code made for one failing case, re-run the complete frozen suite before accepting it; re-run a crashed script to completion before committing its output.
HANDOFF.md §Working rules; every S-### `Done when` runs the full ctest/pytest suite
